sources.title: Prior Analytics, Book I, parts 1–4
sources.author: Aristotle; A. J. Jenkinson translation
sources.version: Hosted English translation, Book I opening
sources.accessScope: Definitions of premise, universal/particular statements, syllogism, and opening first-figure valid/invalid relations; not all syllogistic.
sources.rights: Ancient original and translation/site edition have distinct rights; no translation text bundled.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code; distinguish supplied evidence from inference.
rules.rationale: Project-wide meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes a factual change.

rules.intent: Separate premises from conclusion and use each term consistently; expose implicit premises as assumptions.
rules.rationale: Adapts opening syllogistic definitions to argument review.
exceptions: An unstated premise may be proposed explicitly, but not presented as a supplied fact.

rules.intent: Retain universal/particular scope, negation, modality, and existence assumptions when formalizing.
rules.rationale: Applies the source distinctions while making modern/existential assumptions explicit.
exceptions: When ordinary-language scope is ambiguous, show the alternatives rather than silently selecting one.

rules.intent: Ask whether the conclusion follows if the premises hold, then separately assess support for those premises.
rules.rationale: Operational separation of deductive consequence and factual support.
exceptions: Empirical likelihood and causal claims need their own evidence; a plausible conclusion is not necessarily deduced.

rules.intent: For a disputed inference, construct a possible case where the premises hold and conclusion fails, or give the explicit valid form.
rules.rationale: Project adaptation of valid/invalid form testing, not a complete automatic logic solver.
exceptions: State when the argument falls outside simple categorical syllogistic instead of forcing it into that form.
